dedupe_keys.name: mobile ground based methane measurements at new york state landfills 2021 to 2022

description: This dataset holds methane concentrations measured from a vehicle driving around New York State landfills during three field campaigns in 2021 and 2022. It was produced by Alexandra Catena, Jie Zhang, Margaret J. Schwab and colleagues at the University at Albany, State University of New York, with Roisin Commane and Andrew Hallward-Driemeier of Columbia University, and published on Dryad. Methane was measured with an Aerodyne dual quantum cascade laser spectrometer and a Picarro cavity ring-down analyser, calibrated before and after each deployment against standards traceable to the NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory on the WMO X2004A scale, with clock drift and response time corrected and gaps in one instrument filled from the other. Files are split by year and site and include coordinates and weather from the nearest New York State Mesonet station, such as temperature, pressure and wind. The files, about 4 MB, are free to download from Dryad under a Creative Commons Zero public domain dedication. Caveats: mobile transects give concentrations along roads, not emission rates, and each site was visited only on campaign days. Simulation uses: observed methane plumes to test landfill gas emission estimates and site condition models. Related records: the EDF landfill methane map (data-edf-landfill-methane-map) and GHGSat landfill plumes (data-ghgsat-landfill-methane-plumes) give other emission evidence.
